source.title: Dorsolateral striatum is critical for the expression of surprise-induced enhancements in cue associability

confidence_rationale: Shows that the EXPRESSION of enhanced cue associability depends on dorsolateral striatum within an amygdalo-nigro-striatal circuit that also supports conditioned orienting. Supports a separable write/read structure but weakens any reading of MECH-598 as an amygdala-local mechanism, and ties associability to orienting responses (SD-099 territory).
failure_signatures: Associability enhancement is established without DLS but cannot be expressed without it, so associability is a distributed circuit property, not a variable held in one amygdala-like module.
The same circuit supports learned orienting responses to cues, so an associability effect in REE may be inseparable from orienting (SD-099) unless the orienting read-out is controlled for.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In a three-stage serial prediction task, DLS is critical for expressing, but not establishing, the enhanced cue associability produced by surprise; this extends the amygdalo-nigro-striatal circuit underlying learned orienting responses to associability.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-598's subject is labelled amygdala.aversive_pe_cue_associability. This paper places the read-out in striatum and links associability to conditioned orienting. For REE this is a design warning: SD-099 orienting and MECH-598 associability may share circuitry, so a Q-113 test must separate 'the agent orients to A' from 'the agent learns about A faster'.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Appetitive, rodent. The orienting link is the authors' circuit framing rather than a direct demonstration that associability equals orienting. Recorded mixed because it supports structure and weakens locus.
mapping.source_context: Rat, three-stage serial prediction task, DLS lesions/inactivation

confidence_components.notes: Useful mainly as a design constraint on the V3 test, not as support or refutation.
